/work as a gallery — three layouts

A — grid of cards

Two cards across, each holding its own front/back pair at half width. Densest of the three: seventeen projects fit in about nine rows.

Risk: at 1200px each screenshot ends up ~270px wide, which is page-shape only — you cannot read a nav or a column header. Fine for "this is real", useless for "look what it does".

B — full-width rows

One project per row, the pair at the width it gets on the homepage today. Screenshots stay legible and the page reads as a portfolio rather than a contact sheet.

Risk: it is long. Seventeen of these is a lot of scrolling, and the eleven with no imagery become obvious gaps rather than quiet entries.

C — compact list

Every project is a tight row; the ones with imagery carry a small pair, the ones without are a line of text. Scannable in one screen, and it degrades gracefully — a project with no screenshot does not look broken, it looks brief.

Risk: the least impressive of the three, and it undersells the pairs that are genuinely good. The Horse & Harmony pair deserves more than 260px.
